mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year indicates inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and subsequently negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE < 5% and S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates strong economic growth, which is positive for corporate earnings and thus leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 increases over two consecutive quarters and S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a weakening supply side, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO MoM < -1% and S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing, it indicates a tightening monetary policy to combat inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL is increasing, and S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) suggests a strong labor market, which is positive for consumer spending and thus leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS is increasing and UNRATE is decreasing, and S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates increased demand for new homes, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and thus leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST > 1.2*average of last 12 months and S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 5% month-over-month signals a weakening consumer demand, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS MoM < -5% and S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the cases.
